heading: Standard sparse objectives produce splitting and absorption on hierarchical inputs; objectives like Matryoshka reduce absorption
definition: splitting is produced by the SAE training objective on correlated or hierarchical inputs, so it says little about the model's own units; objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs change or reduce it.
summary: Independent toy, theory and objective-comparison studies find that standard sparse objectives produce absorption or splitting on hierarchical inputs, and that Matryoshka and other objectives cut absorption on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B. For splitting itself in models of this size, most reported drops come from overlapping author groups and the one independent test gives mixed results; no study at any scale tests whether splitting reflects the SAE rather than the model's own units.

source.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: David Chanin; James Wilken-Smith; Tomás Dulka; Hardik Bhatnagar; Satvik Golechha; J. Bloom

original_result.setup: They trained SAEs on toy models with four orthogonal features or twelve features, varying whether a child feature fires only with its parent.
original_result.result: With independent features the SAE recovered one latent per feature, but when the child fired only with its parent, the child latent absorbed the parent direction and the parent latent failed to fire on the child's inputs. The pattern weakened when the child co-occurred with its parent 95% of the time and still appeared in a batch TopK SAE (k=2) with no L1 term; the paper measured absorption, not splitting, and tested no Matryoshka-style objective.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: In a two-Gaussian toy, the SAE loss favoured many features over the ideal two-feature solution.
In a Boolean toy, sparsity always favoured splitting; a minimum-description-length objective avoided it under weak correlation.
A hierarchical SAE had less absorption than a standard SAE with as many top-level latents.
On synthetic hierarchies, ReLU and BatchTopK SAEs showed absorption; matching-pursuit MP-SAE removed it, Matryoshka reduced it.
Matryoshka removed or sharply cut absorption and splitting on toy data and Gemma-2-2B.
Toy SAEs distorted clean hierarchical features; Gemma splitting scores varied with the Matryoshka loss weighting.
Matryoshka and OrtSAE (orthogonality-penalised) both cut absorption well below BatchTopK SAEs on Gemma and Llama.
Masking to decorrelate token co-occurrence improved absorption scores on Pythia-160M, and on Gemma-2-2B at low ℓ0.
Theory shows the L1 dictionary objective imposes splitting and absorption on hierarchical inputs.
Compared with per-sample sparsity alone, Matryoshka, OrtSAE and C2R objectives sharply cut absorption and reduced splitting.
Varying the TopK sparsity budget k switched SAEs between child-feature latents and one shared parent latent.
In a three-concept toy, reconstruction under a rate constraint made splitting codes optimal when concepts co-occurred.
Vector SAEs spread one synthetic manifold feature over 9–171 atoms; group-sparse SASA used one group.
On GPT2-small, Matryoshka beat Top-k on splitting and absorption; MP-SAE did worse.
End-to-end SAEs (output-KL loss) clustered features much less than local SAEs, by a nearest-neighbour similarity proxy.
Standard SAEs mixed co-occurring toy features in their latents; an orthogonality loss recovered the true features.
On Gemma-2-2B, Matryoshka cut absorption to about 0.03, versus 0.29 for BatchTopK, and reduced splitting.
Matryoshka matched toy ground truth in most runs where vanilla SAEs absorbed features.
Toy SAE absorption occurred only with co-occurring features, grew with L1 penalty, vanished with tied weights.
A loose derivation shows the sparsity loss rewards absorption whenever both features co-occur.
In a hierarchical toy, a standard SAE recovered 11 of 20 features; Matryoshka recovered all 20.
Theory derives splitting and absorption from first-order optimality of the dictionary objective.
Splitting rate depended strongly on the learning method: ConSDL split more often than ReLU or TopK.
Under high feature correlation, a minimum-description-length objective also favoured splitting, so some splitting reflects input statistics.
Matryoshka reduced absorption only in some runs and added negative interference between sibling (same-parent) features.
Weighting the losses of Matryoshka's nested latent groups by group size worsened absorption on Gemma-2-2B.
OrtSAE absorption rose from about 0.15 to 0.20 as its orthogonality penalty used more latent chunks.
At higher ℓ0 on Gemma-2-2B, co-occurrence masking worsened the absorption score or left it unchanged.
On Qwen3-8B all objectives gave identical splitting; Gemma-2-2B drops had overlapping confidence intervals.
Splitting conditions depend on raw co-occurrence probabilities, not correlation, in this toy.
When the end-to-end SAE also had to match downstream activations, its clustering-proxy advantage shrank to 0.04.
An orthogonality loss dropped a parent feature, and narrow single-latent SAEs still merged parent and children.
Matryoshka was no better at two locations, and absorption examples remained, though rarer.

The only real-model input manipulation (masking) measures absorption only. C2R's causal account of correlated inputs is theoretical (Lemma 4.1). OrtSAE does not manipulate inputs.

Whether the predicted shift of the absorption phase boundary under Matryoshka holds in real language-model SAEs. It is confirmed only synthetically; real-model comparisons use a confounded firing proxy.
untested.basis: Untested-parts line of arXiv:2609.29551, which cites its rows r24 and r25 (not in this pack).

wording_issues.phrase: splitting is produced by the SAE training objective
wording_issues.issue: Most real-model evidence measures absorption, not splitting. This covers OrtSAE (2509.22033: absorption, composition, clustering and cross-model uniqueness), masking (2604.06495, whose untested line says splitting is not measured) and H-SAE (2506.01197: SAEBench absorption only). The analytic post lw:RxtaNrynuzPf4JePE addresses absorption rather than splitting. 2606.30609 measures splitting directly (Split Num, lower is better), and the outcome depends on the setting. On Qwen3-8B layer 20, Split Num is unchanged at 1.1154 for BatchTopK, Matryoshka, OrtSAE and C2R alike. On Gemma-2-2B layer 12 (Table 8, 5 seeds) it goes from 1.0962 (BatchTopK) to 1.0385-1.0673, with overlapping 95% CIs, while absorption falls from 0.1908 to 0.0656 ± 0.0185 with C2R. Split Num drops in single runs: Llama-3-8B layer 20, 1.1923 to 1.0385 (OrtSAE, C2R) and 1.1154 (Matryoshka) (Table 10); Gemma-2-2B layer 12 TopK and AbsTopK backbones with C2R, 1.3462 to 1.0769 (Table 16); Gemma-2-2B layer 20, 1.3462 to 1.2308-1.2692 (Table 11); 1B-token and Pile runs, 1.1538 to 1.0385-1.0769 (Tables 12-13). The pack shows no rows for Tables 11-13.

2605.14694 finds that the conditions for optimal splitting are raw joint probabilities (co-occurrence), and calls correlation 'at best a proxy'. 2606.06333 gets objective-driven fragmentation (9-171 atoms per feature, per its verdict) for a single multidimensional manifold feature, with no correlation or hierarchy. 2405.08366 gets over-splitting for one binary variable in a two-Gaussian mixture.

wording_issues.phrase: so it says little about the model's own units
wording_issues.issue: No row tests this. 2610.23801's authors read the extra splitting under ConSDL as real finer concepts (verdict reason). 2410.11179 R4 shows that even an MDL objective prefers splitting at high correlation, i.e. some splitting is justified by the data.

wording_issues.phrase: objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs change or reduce it
wording_issues.issue: Several of the effective changes are not objective changes. Tied weights remove absorption in toys (lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN r7; the verdict calls this an architecture change). H-SAE changes architecture plus a loss term (2506.01197). Masking changes the training data (2604.06495). MP-SAE changes the encoder/inference (2506.03093). Some changes increase splitting: ConSDL at 45-55% vs ReLU at 12-37% (2610.23801 r3, r4), and MP-SAE scores worse than Top-k on GPT2-small (2605.07922 r3).

method_sensitivity.what: 2604.06495: the masking gain on Gemma-2-2B is +3.75 at ℓ0=20 (r5) and +1.39 at ℓ0=40 (r6). It reverses at ℓ0=80 (98.969 to 97.322, r7) and is negligible at ℓ0=160 (r8). On Pythia-160M the gain shrinks to +0.57 at ℓ0=160 (r4); the gains are as given in the verdict fixes. 2509.22033 r4: OrtSAE absorption is lower across L0 25-130 (figure-only).

2505.11756 R10 (Gemma-2-2b layer 12, BatchTopK k=40, width 32768, 10 seeds): a balance-Matryoshka loss multiplier of about 0.75 gives a better (lower) SAEBench feature-splitting score than standard Matryoshka (multiplier 1) or a standard SAE (multiplier 0) (figure-only). 2503.17547 R11: group-size loss weighting worsens absorption. 2606.30609: C2R λ=0.1 leaves absorption at 0.1926 vs 0.1985 (t15-l01-abs), and λ=1 leaves Split Num at 1.1154 (t15-l1-split). 2509.22033 (Appendix C text, no row; Gemma-2-2B layer 12, L0=70): OrtSAE absorption rises slightly as chunk count K goes from 4 to 64, from about 0.15 to 0.20, but stays below traditional SAEs at every K. Only the size of the reduction changes.

2606.06333: atoms per circle feature are 36 (ReLU), 44 (TopK), 10 (BatchTopK), 12 (JumpReLU) and 36 (Gated), vs 1 group for SASA. lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN: untied weights absorb while tied weights do not (r2 vs r7). 2610.23801 (4× to 16× expansions, four backbones): 45-55% of consistent 4× atoms have at least 2 consistent 16× counterparts for ConSDL, and 12-37% for ReLU SAEs. TopK fractions are substantially lower than ConSDL's; no TopK number is given in rows, and TopK is not ranked against ReLU (r3-r5). 2605.07922 r3: MP-SAE is worse than Top-k on splitting (GPT2-small, figure-only).

lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN: independent features give no absorption (r1), and perfect co-occurrence gives a parent hole (r2). At 95% co-occurrence, absorption is reduced at L1 5e-3 (r5), but at L1 2e-2 the parent latent fails to fire when both features are active (r6). 2410.11179: MDL avoids splitting at small ρ (R3) but prefers it at large ρ (R4). 2506.03093 varies within-level correlation (0 and 0.3 in rows; 0.6 and 0.9 per its method line). 2604.06495 decorrelates inputs by masking.

lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN: at 95% co-occurrence, absorption is weak at L1 5e-3 (r5) and much stronger at a higher L1 (r6). 2405.08366 r2: the many-feature solution beats the ideal 2-feature solution over a λ sweep. Not in rows, a 2-feature SAE recovers ±μ for 1≤λ≤3.

2606.30609: Split Num drops on Llama-3-8B (1.19 to 1.04, verdict reason) but is unchanged on Qwen3-8B (1.1154 for all objectives). 2604.06495: at ℓ0=80, masking improves Pythia-160M (94.650 to 96.437, r3) but worsens Gemma-2-2B (98.969 to 97.322, r7).

2606.30609, Gemma-2-2B layer 12, L0=100, 5 seeds (Table 8): C2R cuts absorption from 0.1908 to 0.0656 (t8-c2r-abs), but Split Num moves only from 1.0962 to 1.0385, within overlapping CIs (t8-c2r-split). The BatchTopK Split Num for the same Gemma setting is 1.0962 in Table 8 but 1.1154 in Tables 14-15 (t14-ort-split, t15-l1-split). This divergence is specific to that setting: on TopK/AbsTopK backbones, Split Num falls from 1.35 to 1.08 with C2R (verdict reason, t16-topkc2r-split).

lw:zbebxYCqsryPALh8C, 4-layer TinyStories model, for smaller reference SAE sizes only: Matryoshka has higher mean max correlation than same-L0 vanilla SAEs at most attention-output, MLP-output and residual locations (r4). It is not higher at the residual stream before the first block or at the first attention output (r5). No values are given (appendix graphs).

status_amendment.public_note: The status now accounts for shared authors: independent groups reproduce the lower absorption under Matryoshka and other objectives on 2B-8B models, but on those models the clearest drops in splitting itself come from authors of one of the topic's original papers, and the one independent splitting test there gives mixed results. The overall level stays R2, while reduced splitting in 1-10B models is now rated R1.
